rule: A record generates no runtime functions, unlike macros that do (`defdelegate`, `defexception`), whose generated functions are call targets.
spec_gap: Does `defdelegate slug(s), to: MyApp.Util` emit an edge from the generated `MyApp.Facade.slug` to `MyApp.Util.slug` (call_type direct or implicit, high, on the defdelegate line), or is it a declaration with no edge, like def/defstruct?
notes: `title/1` calls `slug(s)`, which the SPEC makes a call target: `MyApp.Facade.slug`, high. But completeness of the case also needs the defdelegate line itself (facade.ex:2): the generated `MyApp.Facade.slug` runs `MyApp.Util.slug(s)`, which is not written as a call but is what the code does at runtime. SPEC does not say whether that is an edge (direct? implicit?), with what caller and line.
